rich_summary: Ghatotkacha, Bhima’s rakshasa son, is slain by Karna using Indra’s divine dart, but in dying he expands his gigantic body and crushes a vast portion of the Kaurava army, destroying an entire Akshauhini. The Pandavas grieve, yet Krishna unexpectedly rejoices. Arjuna questions this strange reaction, and Krishna reveals the strategic truth: Karna has just spent the one irresistible weapon that was destined for Arjuna. Without his natural armor, earrings, and now the celestial dart, Karna is no longer invincible and can eventually be killed. Krishna explains that many earlier events—the deaths or weakening of powerful warriors like Jarasandha, Ekalavya, and others—were also carefully engineered to protect the Pandavas. Dhritarashtra later realizes the same grim logic: Krishna deliberately forced Karna to waste the fatal weapon on Ghatotkacha, turning the rakshasa’s death into a decisive strategic victory.

highlight_spans.why: The dramatic death of Ghatotkacha and the moment he falls after being struck by Indra’s dart, setting the emotional and strategic turning point.
Describes how the dying Ghatotkacha enlarges his body and crushes a huge portion of the Kaurava army, turning his death into a final devastating attack.
The Pandavas mourn while Krishna rejoices, introducing the crucial thematic contrast between emotional loss and strategic foresight.
Krishna explains that Karna’s divine dart—the one weapon capable of killing Arjuna—has now been wasted, revealing why Ghatotkacha’s sacrifice matters.

top_scenes.scene_text: The gigantic Ghatotkacha, pierced by Karna’s celestial dart, grows monstrously large as he falls from the sky and crushes masses of Kaurava soldiers beneath his collapsing body.
Krishna stands on Arjuna’s chariot shouting with fierce joy and dancing in triumph while the grieving Pandavas stare in confusion at Ghatotkacha’s fallen form.
Krishna calmly explaining to Arjuna on the battlefield that Karna has wasted his invincible weapon, while the war rages around them under a dark, smoke-filled sky.
